But model.latest() returns the last list element even when it is None. An in-memory call of model.forecast(history, assumptions) fails at src/aicfinal/model.py line 86 `shares = latest(hist, "diluted_shares")["val"]` with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable`. src/aicfinal/valuation.py line 79 has the same pattern. The 10-K XBRL tags only FY (1,143M) and 9M YTD diluted shares, not Q4. The release shows Q4 diluted shares of 1,147M and Q4 diluted EPS of $32.87, but neither is an XBRL fact. The workaround needs a code fix: e.g. latest() should fall back to the last non-null value (FY2026Q3 1,145M, F-3d172a9372), or the 10-K case should use the FY weighted figure. share_change_qoq itself was set from reported quarterly facts (1,138M/1,142M/1,145M) and is not contaminated by the differenced value. gate_eps silently skips this period because sh is None.
